comment: Liquid Dynamics vessels. profile_mm is the wall's mid-surface from the rim or lip down the inside, through the bottom (and stem) to the edge of the base: [r, y, thickness] in mm, y up from the base. A solid stem is a rod written as r = t/2 (Pappus then gives its volume exactly). cavity_end indexes the cavity's bottom centre. Strength is the Weibull scale of the wall's bending strength under a strike.

vessels.name: Bordeaux wine glass
vessels.description: A machine-made soda-lime red wine glass: tall bowl, 1.2 mm wall, solid stem, 80 mm foot.

provenance.profile_mm: estimated: drawn to a common machine-made Bordeaux glass (height 220 mm, bowl 95 mm, foot 80 mm, 1.1-1.3 mm wall)
provenance.strength_MPa: calibrated: Weibull scale for the few square millimetres a strike bends, set so that a 0.3 m/s knock on a table never breaks the glass, tipping it over sometimes does, a 0.75 m fall onto tile always does and onto carpet rarely (docs/validation.md); fire-polished soda-lime glass is far stronger over small areas than large-area design values of 50-100 MPa (Quinn, NIST SP 960-16; size effect m = 6)
provenance.weibull_modulus: published: annealed soda-lime glass m = 5-8 (Quinn 2007; ASTM C1239 practice)
provenance.capacity_ml: estimated: brimful capacity of the profile, checked by the tests
provenance.fill_ml: published: a standard pour, 5 US fl oz = 148 ml (NIAAA standard drink)

vessels.name: Bordeaux wine bottle
vessels.description: A 750 ml Bordeaux bottle: 300 mm tall, 75 mm body, 3 mm wall, heavy punted base, opened.

provenance.profile_mm: estimated: drawn to the common 750 ml Bordeaux bottle (height 295-305 mm, body 74-76 mm, punt 15-20 mm)
provenance.strength_MPa: estimated: container glass carries handling flaws from the line and the shop, so a little weaker than the stemware above
provenance.capacity_ml: published: brimful capacity of a 750 ml bottle is ~765-775 ml (OIV / EU directive 75/107/EEC measuring container tolerances)
provenance.fill_ml: estimated: a bottle opened and a glass poured
